course.oneline: Using Google's no-code gen AI apps (Workspace with Gemini, Gems, Gemini Notebook, Gemini for Google Cloud) and prompting techniques in daily work; the exam tests which tool fits which need.

key.d: **Google Workspace with Gemini** (exam: Gemini for Google Workspace) puts Gemini inside Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Meet and Slides. Features depend on **Workspace edition**; business and enterprise licences add **enterprise-grade data protection**.

**Zero-shot**: no examples, relies on existing knowledge. **One-shot**: one example to apply to similar cases. **Few-shot**: multiple examples for better task understanding. Techniques can be combined.
**Role prompting** assigns a specific role or persona to shape style, tone and focus. **Prompt chaining** makes each response build on the previous one, refining incrementally.

**Prompt templates** store reusable prompts. **Saved info** is persistent context used across all chats. **Gems** are task-specific assistants with instructions and attached resources; separate chats, nothing spills over.

**Grounding** connects output to verifiable, specific sources. **RAG** retrieves from a knowledge base, then generates: better accuracy, explainability, lower hallucination risk. Offerings: pre-built RAG with **Agent Search**, RAG APIs, Grounding with Google Search.

**Gemini Notebook** is no-code RAG: it answers only from your sources, with **citations**, and says when it can't answer. Shared notebooks give a **single source of truth**; Studio offers Audio Overviews and quizzes.

**Gemini for Google Cloud** does not use your prompts or responses to train models. Portfolio: Gemini Cloud Assist, Gemini in BigQuery, Gemini Code Assist, Colab Enterprise, Databases, Looker, Security.
While experimenting, ask whether a use case is **repeatable** and whether gen AI falls short for lack of **customisation**; raise these with the team. Humans verify outputs (**HITL**).

watch: **Gemini for Google Workspace** (exam guide name) and **Google Workspace with Gemini** (current name) are the same product.
**Gemini Notebook** uses only your sources, not the entire internet; **grounding** is not exclusive to it (Gems, prompts, RAG).
**Saved info** applies to all chats; **Gems** are task-specific; prompt chaining keeps context within one conversation.
No-SQL analysis → **Gemini in BigQuery**; fleet management → Databases; Python/ML → Colab Enterprise; threat containment → Security.

4.1.gist: Course introduction: learn gen AI hands-on with existing apps, and spot use cases worth customising or automating for the team.
points: The best way to grasp gen AI is **hands-on with existing apps**, chatbots included; they don't show every capability but spark ideas.
While experimenting, ask: is this use case **repeatable**? Is gen AI falling short because it lacks **customisation** (output "a bit off")?
Write such cases down and raise them with the team: they have the biggest organisational impact (leading to **Gems**, Gemini Notebook, custom agents).
Course questions: gen AI in your **daily workflow**, techniques to improve prompting, products needing **no development expertise**, and **more automated workflows**.

4.2.gist: Google Workspace with Gemini (exam: Gemini for Google Workspace) puts the Gemini model inside Workspace apps; what each app's features do.
points: **Google Workspace** = cloud productivity and collaboration tools (Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Meet, Slides); available Gemini features depend on your **Workspace edition**.
**Business and enterprise licences** add **enterprise-grade data protection**, extending to Workspace with Gemini and the Gemini app, plus **admin features** to manage usage and access.

**Gemini side panel** works across emails and docs without switching apps; Sheets can **generate formulas**; Slides creates **photorealistic images**; Meet does real-time transcription, translation, summaries.
**Google Vids** drafts videos with "Help me Create". **AppSheet** is a **no-code app builder** (enterprise editions); Gemini in AppSheet builds app structure from natural language.

4.3.gist: Understood.org used Google Workspace with Gemini and the Gemini app to surface trends, build donor profiles and tailor fundraising communications.
points: Research team asks Gemini trend questions and has it **cite its sources**; the team **verifies** the outputs, exports them to a Google Doc, hands off.
The partnerships team then uses Gemini to write **personalised messages** to donors and partners, edited before sending.
Key benefit (knowledge check): **saving time on repetitive tasks** and personalising communications; not eliminating humans, not one-off email writing.
Workspace with Gemini goes beyond content generation to **organisational efficiency and customisation**; humans verify outputs (**HITL**). Gemini also reduces **cognitive load** of context switching.

4.4.gist: Prompting with examples: zero-shot, one-shot and few-shot, practised by classifying a tricky help-desk ticket.
points: **Zero-shot**: a task with **no examples**, relying on existing knowledge. Mnemonic: "Just tell it what you want."
**One-shot**: **one example** to learn from and apply to similar cases. Mnemonic: "Guide it with a single example."
**Few-shot**: **multiple examples** for better task understanding and performance. Mnemonic: "Show, don't tell." You can **combine** techniques.
Exercise "Help desk hero": classify a support ticket with each technique and reflect on how the **number of examples** changes prompt, result and trade-offs.

4.5.gist: Role prompting: assigning the model a specific role or persona to shape the style, tone and focus of its responses.
points: **Role prompting** guides an LLM by assigning a **specific role or persona** (business analyst, Shakespearean actor, helpful customer-service agent).
It shapes **style, tone and focus**: the model acts as an **expert or character**, so content is tailored.
Template: "You are a [persona]. Please write a [task]." Bonus: rerun the same task with a different persona and compare.
Role prompting is also the recommended way to write **Gem instructions**.

4.6.gist: Prompt chaining: each response builds on the previous one, step by step, to reach more complex and nuanced results.
points: **Prompt chaining**: each response **builds on the previous one**, like a conversation; in Gemini, earlier prompts affect later ones (shared context).
Method: start with a **broad initial prompt**, follow up with clarifications, specifics or a different format, then refine **incrementally** rather than in one request.
General definition: a task split into a **sequence of prompts** where each output feeds the next step; a chat conversation is one way.
Exercise "The chain reaction": e.g. a Tokyo business-trip itinerary, then follow-ups adding hotels near the conference centre or day trips.

4.7.gist: Levels of reusing prompts without code, from prompt templates to chaining, Gemini Advanced, Saved info and Gems.
points: Simple to tailored: **prompt templates** (saved in a Google Doc or Sheet), chaining in one thread (name and pin chats), Gemini Advanced, Saved info, Gems.
**Gemini Advanced**: upgraded Gemini for coding, logical reasoning, nuanced instructions, creative collaboration; you can set **data retention** and delete conversation history.
**Saved info** (set in Settings) is used **across all chats**: context remembered without full conversation history influencing answers, e.g. a sales rep practising pitches.
**Gems** give **task-specific** context when Saved info is too broad. Rule: chaining = in-conversation context; Saved info = global persistent; Gems = task-specific assistants.

4.8.gist: Gems as personalised AI assistants inside Gemini: their three benefits, how to build them, and best practices.
points: Three benefits: **personalised responses**, **streamlined workflows**, and **reset context**: multiple separate chats with one Gem, nothing spills over between them.
Use Google's **pre-made Gems** or create a **custom Gem**, whose instructions prompt the agent how to act; role prompting fits well here.
**Attach documents and resources** for a focused knowledge base, e.g. a code-reviewer Gem with the project style guide, so feedback is **grounded**.
Best practices: be **clear and specific**, provide examples, **refine instructions over time**, and think about how users will interact with it.

4.9.gist: Grounding connects outputs to verifiable sources; RAG retrieves external knowledge before generating; Gemini Notebook offers RAG without code.
points: **Grounding**: connecting output to **verifiable, specific sources**, critical for trust and reliability. No-code: attach resources to a Gem, or documents in Gemini prompts.
**RAG**: **retrieve** relevant information from a knowledge base (often via semantic search or vector databases), embed it in the prompt, then **generate**.

Versus model only: latest external knowledge, much lower **hallucination** risk. Benefits: accuracy and relevance, **explainability and transparency**, extending LLM capabilities (constraining output).
Exam guide distinguishes grounding with **first-party enterprise data** (your own), **third-party data** (external datasets) and **world data** (public knowledge, e.g. Google Search).

4.10.gist: Gemini Notebook: an AI-first notebook grounded only in your own documents; its editions, workflow, use cases and difference from Gems.
points: **Gemini Notebook**: AI-first virtual research assistant on Gemini models; uses **only your sources**, gives **citations**, and says it can't answer when sources don't cover it.
**Gemini Notebook Plus** adds capacity, customisable response length/style, usage analytics; **Gemini Notebook Enterprise** adds compliance, admin, chosen-collaborator sharing, **IAM roles**.
Gems suit general tasks and workflows; Gemini Notebook suits **deep understanding of a specific set of information** (hyper-focused, interactive learning, source-based answers).
Sources: PDFs, text, Markdown, audio, Google Drive, website and YouTube links, pasted text. **Studio panel**: **Audio Overviews** (two AI hosts), Flashcards, Quizzes.

4.11.gist: A venture capital firm uses a shared Gemini Notebook to break information silos and analyse investments from a single source of truth.
points: Problem: too much data, missed insights, documents scattered across departments (**information silos**). Solution: a **shared Gemini Notebook** workspace as a **single source of truth**.
Uses: **targeted questions**, analysing specific aspects (e.g. a startup's user acquisition costs), and to **uncover hidden connections** (early adoption versus long-term success).
Shared notebooks: build understanding together, produce collaborative summaries and reports, spot **connections and contradictions** across perspectives, stay up to date.
True/false: Gemini Notebook doesn't use the entire internet; it can create **quizzes**; it isn't for creative stories; **grounding** isn't exclusive to it.

4.12.gist: Gemini for Google Cloud: Gemini built into Google Cloud products for cloud, software and data roles, with enterprise data protection.
points: **Gemini for Google Cloud** does NOT use your prompts or Gemini's responses **to train models**; standard Google Cloud **enterprise protections** apply.
**Gemini Cloud Assist**: design, manage, optimise apps using environment, metrics and logs. **Gemini Code Assist**: an **AI pair programmer**, 20+ programming languages.
**Gemini in BigQuery**: analysis regardless of SQL experience. **Gemini in Colab Enterprise**: Python in notebooks. **Gemini in Databases**: natural language, fleet of databases.
**Gemini in Looker**: understand data, create visualisations, generate reports. **Gemini in Security**: detect, contain, stop threats; analyses **attack paths**; summarises threat actors' **TTPs**.

4.13.gist: Cymbal Retail (fictitious) uses Gemini in BigQuery with function calling so marketers query data in natural language without writing SQL.
points: Problem: marketers lack SQL skills and depend on the **data analytics team**, creating a **bottleneck** that delays insights.
Solution: **Gemini in BigQuery with function calling** in a user-friendly app; Gemini **translates the question into SQL**, retrieves and presents the data.
Three benefits: **increased agility**, **improved collaboration** (analysts freed for strategic work), and **enhanced data literacy** for business users.
Distractors: fleet management → Gemini in Databases; Python/ML → Colab Enterprise; threat containment → Gemini in Security. Theme: "**democratise data access**".
